parts.name: Mounting base
parts.description: The mounting plate anchors the arm to its work surface. Loads from every moving joint pass through this plate into the support below.
parts.detail: The outer holes take mounting fasteners. The circular seat in the center locates the base bearing.
parts.prompt: Orbit above the plate to see the mounting holes around the central bearing.

parts.name: Base motor
parts.description: The base motor supplies rotation around the vertical axis. Turning the base changes which direction the entire arm faces.
parts.detail: The square black housing stays seated above the plate. Torque leaves the motor through the central shaft.
parts.prompt: Change Base rotation in the motion lab and watch the gripper sweep sideways.

parts.name: Lower link
parts.description: This short structural member extends from the shoulder assembly. Its bosses provide substantial material around the pivot holes.
parts.detail: The open pockets remove material between the bosses while leaving continuous edges along the link.
parts.prompt: Isolate the link and rotate it edge-on to see the thickness of the machined plate.

parts.name: Shoulder motor
parts.description: The shoulder motor sits at the first lifting joint. It supplies torque to raise the links and the tool mounted beyond them.
parts.detail: The shoulder has to support more torque when the tool reaches farther horizontally from its pivot.
parts.prompt: View the arm from behind to see the motor housing and its connection to the shoulder.

parts.name: Lift arm
parts.description: The diagonal lift arm carries the elbow away from the shoulder. Its length sets the distance between those two joint axes.
parts.detail: The large circular bosses surround the pivots. The webs between the openings carry loads along the arm.
parts.prompt: Raise Shoulder lift in the motion lab and follow the circular path of the elbow.

parts.name: Upper drive
parts.description: This motor travels with the upper linkage. It brings a drive close to the wrist carriage, adding mass that the shoulder must also carry.
parts.detail: Look for the black motor body between two metal end caps and the short coupling beside it.
parts.prompt: Orbit to the back of the arm to distinguish the upper drive from the wrist actuator.

parts.name: Upper return link
parts.description: The upper return link runs from the elbow back toward the wrist carriage. Pivoting it changes the wrist position relative to the elbow.
parts.detail: Its repeated openings reduce moving mass. The material around each end provides a seat for the joint hardware.
parts.prompt: Move Elbow bend in the motion lab and watch the wrist follow the far end of this link.

parts.name: Wrist actuator
parts.description: The compact wrist actuator sits directly behind the gripper. It changes tool orientation at the end of the arm.
parts.detail: The drive and gripper are separate assemblies. Rotating a tool and closing its fingers are distinct movements.
parts.prompt: Compare Wrist swivel and Jaw opening in the motion lab. Notice which movement changes the finger spacing.

parts.name: Wrist link
parts.description: The wrist link carries the tool assembly forward from the wrist bearing. Its two end bosses connect the bearing and the actuator.
parts.detail: One end carries a ring of fasteners. The larger boss at the other end sits beside the tool drive.
parts.prompt: Select Isolate part and compare the two ends of the link.

parts.name: Parallel gripper
parts.description: The gripper is the tool that contacts an object. Paired finger linkages bring the opposing pads together to grasp it.
parts.detail: The dark pads are the contact surfaces. The small pivot pins guide the finger links as the opening changes.
parts.prompt: Adjust Jaw opening in the motion lab and watch the pads approach each other.

questions.ask: Which part transfers the arm’s loads into the work surface?
questions.why: The mounting base provides the fixed connection between the moving mechanism and the bench.

questions.ask: Which motor turns the entire arm about its vertical axis?
questions.why: The base motor changes the arm’s heading. The shoulder motor acts at the lifting joint.

questions.ask: Find the diagonal member that carries the elbow away from the shoulder.
questions.why: The lift arm spans the shoulder and elbow pivots. Its length sets their separation.

questions.ask: Which component turns the tool directly behind the gripper?
questions.why: The wrist actuator sets the tool’s orientation. The finger mechanism controls the jaw opening.

questions.ask: Which part makes contact with the object being picked up?
questions.why: The parallel gripper holds the object between its two contact pads.
